answer.diagnosis: The shortcut is a small marker patch in the top-left corner, at image rows 1-3 and columns 1-3. That spot is far from the central blob, so blob size cannot explain it. Yet almost every structured first-layer unit has large-magnitude weights there (about 45-99 in absolute value, against roughly ±30 for noise weights elsewhere). Units 1, 3, 7, 8, 13, 18, 20, 24, 27 and 28 have strongly positive weights on the patch. These are also the units with positive centre/ring blob detectors. Units 11, 12, 16, 17, 19, 21, 25, 26 and 29 (and more weakly 31) have strongly negative weights on the patch. These carry the opposite-sign blob templates. The patch weights share the sign of each unit's blob-size template, so a bright corner patch pushes the network toward one class just as a large blob would. This points to a corner-patch feature that was correlated with the label during training. The genuine size features are the ring and disc patterns over the central rows 5-18, and they are left untouched. The fix is to zero the corner-patch weights in every first-layer unit.
